### P13 "Depth Dither" (ISF Shader) · Fragment

description: Bayer 4x4 ordered dither with depth-scaled strength. Near pixels remain smooth; far pixels are quantised to `levels` values per channel (black and white included) with classic Gameboy / early-PC dither stipple. A nostalgic lo-fi haze for backgrounds. Depth weight 0 applies the full effect everywhere.; categories: Post-process, Stylise; inputs: inputImage:image, camera:uniform, dither:float=0.2, depthWeight:float=1, depthScale:float=30, levels:float=6

### P15 "Depth Micro AO" (ISF Shader) · Fragment

description: Fast single-pass ambient occlusion. Samples eight neighbours at a user radius, counts how many rise more than `bias` above the tangent plane of the current pixel (normal-oriented hemisphere, with a range check), and darkens proportionally. Not as clean as GTAO (see the Multi-pass wave) but cheap, punchy, and single-pass.; categories: Post-process, Lighting; inputs: inputImage:image, camera:uniform, radius:float=8, bias:float=0.01, intensity:float=1.2

59 lines, not listed: the process was created from the library file `<LIBRARY>:packages/score-csf-testers/shaderlib/depth/Depth Micro AO.fs`.

### P16 "Depth Contact Shadow" (ISF Shader) · Fragment

description: Contact shadow: raymarches the scene depth along a light direction for a few steps and shadows fragments whose ray hits closer geometry. Adds the tight contact darkening that regular shadow maps miss. Purely depth-based — no shadow map needed.; categories: Post-process, Lighting; inputs: inputImage:image, camera:uniform, lightDir:point3D=[-0.5,-1,-0.3], rayLength:float=0.5, stepCount:long=8, thickness:float=0.2, strength:float=0.7
